content.title: As it happened: Speed record broken as fan favourite puts on a masterclass at Paris-Roubaix 2026
content.text: Refresh The media has, understandably, been focused on defending three time champion, Mathieu van der Poel (Alpecin-Premier Tech) and world champion, Tadej Pogačar (UAE Team Emirates-XRG) before the start of this race. 2026-04-12T06:38:16.759ZBonjour, and welcome to Cyclingnews' live report of the 123rd running of the men's Paris-Roubaix. Otherwise known as the 'Hell of the North'. 2026-04-12T08:31:02.206ZSign on is well underway for the riders after the team presentation last night. There is just over half an hour until the riders get racing. (Image credit: Getty Images) 2026-04-12T08:36:38.918ZPogačar believes that he may not need to get away solo to take the Hell of the North...>>> ‘I can pull off some kind of good sprint’ – Does Tadej Pogačar even need to arrive alone to win Paris-Roubaix? (Image credit: Getty Images) 2026-04-12T08:51:44.435ZJust under 15 minutes to the official start. The riders have just started the neutral zone in Compiègne, (Image credit: Getty Images) 2026-04-12T08:55:05.218ZJust over 5km to the official start. 🚩The peloton leaves Compiègne, Paris-Roubaix 2026 is underway!🚩Le peloton s’élance de Compiègne. C’est parti pour #ParisRoubaix 2026 ! pic.twitter.com/DSVVG5d0IhApril 12, 2026 2026-04-12T09:03:00.853ZAs we wait for the start, why not have a go at our little quiz we put together! Can you name every podium from the last decade? I'll give you a clue, Van der Poel is in a few of them! (Image credit: Luc Claessen/Getty Images) 2026-04-12T09:03:21.279ZJust 1km to the official start. 2026-04-12T09:06:32.348ZThere will be a delayed start as there are some mechanicals. 2026-04-12T09:07:37.630ZFabian Lienhard (Tudor) makes it back into the peloton. 2026-04-12T09:08:36.297Z 258.3km to go! 2026-04-12T09:09:47.928ZNickolas Zukowsky (Pinarello-Q36.5) is one of the first riders to attack. 2026-04-12T09:10:30.073ZVan der Poel and three of his teammates are right at the back of the peloton. 2026-04-12T09:13:00.101ZSilvan Dillier (Alpecin-Premier Tech) and a few other big names just slipping into the early move. That sees it dragged back, though. The former Swiss champion was second in this race behind the great Peter Sagan. 2026-04-12T09:14:25.274ZThree riders get away from Unibet Rose Rockets, Bahrain Victorious and NSN. They have a pretty decent gap on the chasing group and then the peloton. 2026-04-12T09:17:14.413Z10km of racing done and the average speed is a staggering 57kph! 2026-04-12T09:17:28.180ZThe leading trio have 15" on the peloton. 2026-04-12T09:19:57.944ZRear puncture for Nils Politt (UAE Team Emirates-XRG). 2026-04-12T09:21:28.174ZThe break is Matevž Govekar (Bahrain Victorious), Riley Sheehan (NSN) and Martijn Rasenberg (Unibet Rose Rockets). They still have 15" gap. Several riders in the gap. 2026-04-12T09:25:52.794ZThe leaders have been joined by a rider from Decathlon-CMA CGM. But the gap has dropped to just 5". 2026-04-12T09:26:29.523ZNew attacks leaving the front of the peloton. 2026-04-12T09:26:48.179ZCees Bol (Decathlon-CMA CGM) is the man who joins the leaders. 2026-04-12T09:31:06.539ZBreakaway caught! 2026-04-12T09:31:59.230ZNew attacks go straight away, though. Led by Bahrain Victorious and Decathlon-CMA CGM. Yves Lampaert (Soudal-Quickstep) trying to be stealthy and get into the break. 2026-04-12T09:33:47.614ZThe two clear are Alessandro Borgo (Bahrain Victorious) and the very talented Stan Dewulf (Decathlon-CMA CGM). (Image credit: Getty Images) 2026-04-12T09:35:06.136ZModern Adventure leading a new move but too many follow and that gets nowhere. 2026-04-12T09:36:17.778ZFlanders-Baloise and XDS-Astana try to get involved, but they are quickly brought back. 2026-04-12T09:36:46.675ZIt is just wave after wave of attacks in the peloton. Dewulf and Borgo are still clear by about 5", though. 2026-04-12T09:38:07.924ZSlovakian champion, Lukáš Kubiš (Unibet Rose Rockets) and Matthew Brennan (Visma-Lease a Bike) are two standout names right at the very back of the peloton. Brennan finished 44th on debut last year after showing very good legs in support of Van Aert. 2026-04-12T09:38:39.805ZModern Adventure get a rider across to Dewulf and Borgo. 2026-04-12T09:39:24.359ZA huge attack comes from the peloton and that spells an end to the breakaway yet again. 2026-04-12T09:41:07.643ZNSN lead a new move and is caught by a few others including Asian and Kazakhstani champion, Yevgeniy Fedorov (XDS-Astana). But, again, nothing doing. 2026-04-12T09:43:08.222ZTomáš Kopecký and Matyáš Kopecký both riding for Unibet Rose Rockets. The two brothers also have their sister, Julia Kopecký racing for SD Worx-Protime. An amazing day for the Kopecký family. 2026-04-12T09:46:51.974ZVan Aert, Laporte and Ganna, among others, coming back into the peloton after several riders stop for a nature break. 2026-04-12T09:52:26.093ZEmīls Liepiņš (Pinarello-Q36.5) is one of the riders who launches a new move but, again, nothing doing. 2026-04-12T09:53:13.789ZFlanders-Baloise launches a new move with Zukowsky and a Tudor rider following but some of the big teams are now getting involved with UAE Team Emirates-XRG starting to control things. 2026-04-12T09:56:20.219ZA large group have a decent gap including Kamil Małecki and Zukowsky from Pinarello-Q36.5. 2026-04-12T09:56:44.958ZVisma-Lease a Bike try to get a man in the break and this may spell the end for this latest move. 2026-04-12T09:59:28.633ZA new move goes and Tadej Pogačar himself is right in the mix for the breakaway with 50km to the first cobbled sector. 2026-04-12T10:00:08.544ZPogačar sits up and more moves go yet again. 2026-04-12T10:04:18.063Z25 years since Servais Knaven won this race. Today, his daughter, Mirre of EF Education-Oatly, races the same cobbles...>>> A mud-bath, an over-inflated spare tyre, and a domestique holding the cobblestone trophy – Servais Knaven relives his iconic Paris-Roubaix victory 25 years on (Image credit: Getty Images) 2026-04-12T10:05:15.224ZSo many attacks but nothing is getting away. With this strong tailwind, there is a very big chance that there will be no breakaway at all today. 2026-04-12T10:07:54.276ZGroupama-FDJ United now getting involved in the latest moves. Bahrain Victorious and several Modern Adventure riders also at the front. No gap formed yet, though. 2026-04-12T10:12:31.547Z 200km to go 2026-04-12T10:14:43.370ZLotto-Intermarche get a solo rider clear but he has a long long line leading the peloton. 54kph average speed so far after just over an hour. 2026-04-12T10:16:59.108ZThe moves are just utterly ridiculous. So many moves as Visma-Lease a Bike, Ineos Grenadiers and UAE Team Emirates-XRG are trying to get into the break for the first time. (Image credit: Getty Images) 2026-04-12T10:17:18.700ZFedorov tries to go, yet again. Flying at about 70kph! 2026-04-12T10:24:04.361ZThe peloton is stretched right out in a massive line and some splits re starting to appear. Van der Poel and Pogačar not in it but lots of UAE riders as well as Oliver Naesen (Decathlon-CMA CGM) and Mads Pedersen (Lidl-Trek). Previous winner, John Degenkolb (Picnic-PostNL) and former podium sitter Yves Lampaert (Soudal-QuickStep) also in this huge group. 🖖 The peloton is split in 2 ! Cassure dans le peloton ! ⛓️‍💥#ParisRoubaix 😈 pic.twitter.com/K3kXNttSwRApril 12, 2026 2026-04-12T10:25:28.482ZThere's a lot of panic in the peloton with Visma-Lease a Bike frantically riding on the front. More riders trying to bridge the gap between the peloton and the break. Another Visma rider now kick clear and it is down to Alpecin-Premier Tech and Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe leading the chase. 2026-04-12T10:26:26.566ZPogačar coming back to the peloton after a nature break with Mick van Dijke (Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe). He has a lot of teammates in the front group. Very interesting situation. 2026-04-12T10:26:45.430ZDillier closes things down with Van der Poel in his wheel and the peloton is back together again. 2026-04-12T10:29:23.408ZA brief hiatus in attacks comes and goes as another move starts, led by Groupama-FDJ United. 2026-04-12T10:30:20.024ZPogačar and Ganna still out the back with the world champion now in the wind. A small moment where the cars weren't with them. But now they get back in. 🏁 184km🚴🏻‍♂️🚴🏻‍♂️🚴🏻‍♂️🚴🏻‍♂️🚴🏻‍♂️🚴🏻‍♂️🚴🏻‍♂️🚗All back together and riders who had stopped, like Tadej Pogačar, are returning to the bunch.Le peloton s'est reformé et des coureurs qui s'étaient arrêtés, comme Tadej Pogacar, retrouvent leur place. #ParisRoubaix 😈 pic.twitter.com/3mb9v0QVY2April 12, 2026 2026-04-12T10:31:07.976ZCofidis tried a new move and, for a moment, it looked like he'd be allowed to go. A few more saw this as a chance and the fight gets going all over again. 2026-04-12T10:33:56.294Z20km to go until the first cobbled sector, the Troisvilles à Inchy. 2026-04-12T10:35:01.937Z 180km to go 2026-04-12T10:42:31.695ZA few riders having to unclip right at the back of the peloton. But no-one goes down. 2026-04-12T10:43:11.144ZThe pace rockets in the peloton with just over 10km to the first sector of the day. Sector 30, Troisvilles à Inchy. 2026-04-12T10:45:22.322ZEnjoying our live race coverage? Subscribe to Cyclingnews for an all-access pass to our unrivalled reporting of WorldTour racing, bike tech and exclusive in-depth features. Plus, access to the Cyclingnews app to follow the action on-the-go! Find out more. 2026-04-12T10:47:10.685Z 170km to go 2026-04-12T10:50:43.574ZIneos Grenadiers now appears on the front of the peloton for Ganna. 2026-04-12T10:51:05.899ZSo, no breakaway today. The peloton will hit the cobbles all together. 2026-04-12T10:52:01.652ZVisma-Lease a Bike, Uno-X Mobility, Decathlon-CMA CGM, Ineos Grenadiers, Alpecin-Premier Tech and UAE Team Emirates-XRG all on the front of the peloton with 165km to go. 2026-04-12T10:52:58.976ZBike change for Niklas Märkl (Pinic-PostNL). A nightmare time to get a mechanical with about 3km to the cobbles. 2026-04-12T10:54:58.593Z Sector 30, first cobbles Onto the sector 30, Troisvilles à Inchy. The pace is extremely high and, leading onto it, is Edoardo Affini (Visma-Lease a Bike) and Josh tarling (Ineos Grenadiers). (Image credit: Getty Images) 2026-04-12T10:55:26.893Z Crash! 2026-04-12T10:55:49.682ZTarling flicking his elbow, he doesn't want to lead for too long. 2026-04-12T10:57:07.564ZConnor Swift (Ineos Grenadiers) and Matthias Vacek (Lidl-Trek) moving to the front too on the early cobbles. 2026-04-12T10:57:46.311ZSeveral punctures on this first sector of cobbles with Lorenzo Milesi (Movistar) being one of them. 2026-04-12T10:58:34.327ZStafan Bissegger (Decathlon-CMA CGM) rolled off the front but, as they leave the cobbles, he sits up with an XDS-Astana rider going over the top. 2026-04-12T10:58:51.792ZMore mechanicals and punctures very early on. 2026-04-12T10:59:26.352ZMike Teunissen (XDS-Astana) is the rider who is solo out front. 2026-04-12T11:00:07.929ZSo many mechanicals and punctures with various teams involved. 2026-04-12T11:01:12.482ZJonas Abrahamsen (Uno-X Mobility) was one of the riders caught out. 2026-04-12T11:02:27.614ZPuncture for Mads Pedersen (Lidl-Trek) and he stops for a bike change. Lidl-Trek said that their new special double inner tube/tubeless tyres were puncture proof. The first cobbled sector proves otherwise. 2026-04-12T11:03:14.010Z Sector 29, Viesly à Quiévy Teunissen leads onto the Viesly à Quiévy sector with about 10" on the peloton. Pedersen 38" out the back. 2026-04-12T11:04:06.889ZPedersen trying to quickly make his way through the cars but is being kicked about all over the pave. 2026-04-12T11:04:21.424ZSo much wasted energy for the former world champion. 2026-04-12T11:04:55.693ZUAE Team Emirates-XRG leading the peloton with Pogačar in fourth wheel. 2026-04-12T11:05:12.860ZMolano leading the peloton and Teunissen is caught. (Image credit: Getty Images) 2026-04-12T11:06:27.570ZThey leave sector 29. Pedersen had to negotiate a few stopped cars who were servicing riders. He joins William Blume Levy (Uno-X Mobility) at the back of the peloton. So many riders stopping with issues. Including Toon Aerts (Lotto-Intermarche). 2026-04-12T11:07:17.087Z Sector 28, Quiévy à Fontaine 2026-04-12T11:08:16.802ZPedersen is back in the peloton. A teammate will now come back for him to try and move him up but he needs to try and stay calm. Something I would definitely be struggling with in his situation. Fortunately, I only have to do it on Pro Cycling Manager! 2026-04-12T11:08:49.402ZThe riders are surrounded by the yellow flowers of the Oil Seed Rape fields. 2026-04-12T11:09:10.996ZFront puncture for former Tour of Flanders winner, Kasper Asgreen (EF Education-EasyPost). 2026-04-12T11:11:08.404ZMechanical for Titouan Fontaine (Groupama-FDJ United). (Image credit: Getty Images) 2026-04-12T11:12:05.607ZUAE Team Emirates-XRG, Alpecin-Premier Tech and Soudal-Quickstep leading the peloton as they finish sector 28. 2026-04-12T11:15:00.052ZMechanical for Wout Van Aert! He has Owain Doull coming back for him. Bike change for Abrahamsen as well. A UAE Team Emirates-XRG rider with an issue too. 2026-04-12T11:16:24.886Z Sector 27, Viesly à Briastre 2026-04-12T11:17:02.925ZAntonio Morgado (UAE Team Emirates-XRG) leads the peloton now. Pogačar is right up at the front with Florian Vermeersch. 2026-04-12T11:17:41.760ZArnaud De Lie (Lotto-Intermarche) out of the back. 2026-04-12T11:19:23.167ZSector 27 done and very dusted. The dust cloud is huge. 2026-04-12T11:21:02.433Z Sector 26, Briastre 2026-04-12T11:21:46.597ZIssues for Lampaert now as well. He's out the back on the Briaste sector as the head of the bunch leaves that sector. 2026-04-12T11:24:16.850ZGroups all over the road with Kubis being one of the riders caught out. 2026-04-12T11:24:50.970ZHuge gap between the front group and the second. Mikkel Bjerg leading the way for UAE, now. 2026-04-12T11:25:11.625ZPuncture for Lukáš Kubiš. 2026-04-12T11:26:04.515ZBjerg is going flat out on the front of the peloton. The team of the world champion are destroying the peloton. 2026-04-12T11:28:01.304ZLots of Visma and Ineos riders in the second group that are over 30" down. Molano and Oliveira in that group as well after doing their job for UAE. 2026-04-12T11:28:56.492ZThe pace eases a bit and more teams come to the front of what is left of the peloton. 2026-04-12T11:30:28.379Z Sector 25, Solesmes à Haussy 2026-04-12T11:31:54.372ZThere's a bit of crosswind on this sector. Pogačar in second wheel. Van der Poel in about seventh wheel. Van Aert, Pedersen and Ganna all poorly placed with the latter right at the back of the peloton. 2026-04-12T11:36:01.291ZPuncture for Per Strand Hagenes (Visma-Lease a Bike). He drops out of the front peloton. 2026-04-12T11:36:59.293Z Sector 24, Saulzoir à Verchain-Maugré 2026-04-12T11:38:02.071ZGanna still at the back with Tibor Del Grosso (Alpecin-Premier Tech) and Marco Haller (Tudor) as Morgado is dropped. 2026-04-12T11:39:36.065ZJonathan Milan (Lidl-Trek), Biniam Girmay (NSN) and Jasper Philipsen (Alpecin-Premier Tech) all looking good early doors. 2026-04-12T11:41:41.631ZRasmus Tiller (Uno-X Mobility) leads his team's train as Abrahamsen is in the second group. 2026-04-12T11:42:29.711ZBjerg back on the front of the peloton. 2026-04-12T11:43:57.852Z Sector 23, Verchain-Maugré à Quérénaing 2026-04-12T11:44:51.649Z Crash! 2026-04-12T11:45:59.723ZTarling coming down after a frustrating season so far...>>> ‘I feel dead fit but just slow’ – Josh Tarling lacking top-end power for Paris-Roubaix (Image credit: Getty Images) 2026-04-12T11:47:38.924Z Sector 22, Quérénaing à Maing 2026-04-12T11:48:01.214ZTurner just about to get back on as they start this three start sector. 2026-04-12T11:49:11.731Z Puncture for Pogačar (Image credit: Getty Images) 2026-04-12T11:50:37.684ZPogačar looks very uncomfortable on the Shimano neutral bike. Alpecin-Premier Tech and Visma-Lease a Bike lead the front peloton. 2026-04-12T11:51:03.364ZPuncture for former winner, Dylan van Baarle (Soudal-Quickstep). 2026-04-12T11:52:44.750Z Sector 21, Maing à Monchaux-sur-Écaillon Pogačar getting very frustrated with no team car near him yet. All his riders drop back apart from Vermeersch. 2026-04-12T11:53:21.929ZPuncture for Dillier. 2026-04-12T11:54:18.811ZPogačar is about 45" down on the now Visma led peloton. Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe also leading the bunch with Alpecin-Premier Tech. 2026-04-12T11:54:46.320ZPogačar finally has a car who has come to the middle of the group. They're very panicked. 2026-04-12T11:55:19.737ZBike change for Pogačar. He shouts at the TV moto to get out of the way. He seems very rattled. 2026-04-12T11:57:48.012ZMorgado is now with Pogačar and now Politt is dropping back, too. He is now 45" behind the peloton. 2026-04-12T11:58:46.464ZIt is the longest gap between sectors now, so a good opportunity for UAE to bring things back together again. 2026-04-12T11:59:46.296ZBjerg and Politt drop back for Pogačar. They are frantically chasing for the world champion. 2026-04-12T12:00:40.195ZThe pace is very high in both groups. Pogačar is now 35" off the back of the peloton that is led by Visma-Lease a Bike and Alpecin-Premier Tech. 2026-04-12T12:06:34.023Z Sector 20, Haveluy à Wallers A few years ago, Visma-Lease a Bike detonated the race on this sector. Now, they are working with Alpecin-Premier Tech with a 20" lead over the Pogačar group. Pinarello-Q36.5 doing a lot of work in the bunch as well for Fred Wright. Ineos Grenadiers also well placed. 2026-04-12T12:07:13.741ZPogačar down to just Politt in the chase group. If he has an issue on this four star sector, that could be that for the world champion. 2026-04-12T12:08:20.814ZPhilipsen leading the peloton ahead of Van der Poel out front as Pogačar is doing it on his own and is now 30" out the back. 2026-04-12T12:09:08.448Z Attack! The three time winner goes all in with 103km to go! This is the best way to completely kill off the chances of Pogačar. 2026-04-12T12:10:10.705ZVan der Poel is not going full, yet. He has Laurence Pithie (Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe) on his wheel. Philipsen, Pedersen, Van Aert, Hoole, Laporte, Bissegger and a few others. 2026-04-12T12:10:47.959ZOff sector 20 and Van der Poel looks around to ask for help. Will anyone give it with 7km to go to the Arenberg? 2026-04-12T12:11:38.311ZThe answer is yes. Van Aert comes through with Teunissen and Hoole. Van der Poel looking very twitchy. 18" back to Pogačar. 2026-04-12T12:12:52.338ZInto the final 100km and Pogačar has a long line of the domestiques of his main rivals on his wheel. 2026-04-12T12:13:53.679ZThe front group has eased dramatically with a lot of looking around. Gianni Vermeersch (Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe) comes back to the front. 2026-04-12T12:14:38.865ZPogačar joins the second group on the road and is now about 10" off the back of the front of the race as they head to the Arenberg. 2026-04-12T12:16:22.205ZFlorian Vermeersch drops back and drags Tadej Pogačar back into the lead group. Vermeersch straight to the front. 2026-04-12T12:17:46.827Z Sector 19, Trouée d'Arenberg 2026-04-12T12:18:37.985ZPogačar having to make another effort to move up as Brennan sits up and Van Aert leads onto the cobbles. 2026-04-12T12:19:30.095ZHuge crowds on the trench today as the riders battle to try and move up off the main racing line. Van Aert and Van der Poel well placed. (Image credit: Getty Images) 2026-04-12T12:19:57.563Z Multiple crashes 2026-04-12T12:20:46.735Z Bike change for Van der Poel 2026-04-12T12:21:16.979ZDel Grosso is taking the wheel off his bike and puts it on his leader's bike. 2026-04-12T12:22:31.689ZVan der Poel is now 1'30" behind the lead group of seven that includes Van Aert and Pogačar. 2026-04-12T12:23:36.426Z Puncture 2026-04-12T12:24:27.630ZVan der Poel finally gets the bike change from his team car and leaves the Arenberg. He actually looks remarkably calm. 2026-04-12T12:25:25.622ZLeaders:Tadej Pogačar (UAD)Wout Van Aert (TVL)Chrisophe Laporte (TVL)Mads Pedersen (LTK)Jasper Stuyven (SOQ)Laurence Pithie (RBH)Stefan Bissegger (DCT) (Image credit: Getty Images) 2026-04-12T12:27:48.970Z Sector 18, Wallers à Hélesmes Van der Poel is now closing a bit. 1'58" down as Pogačar pushes the pace out front. 2026-04-12T12:29:02.240Z25" between the lead group and the first chase group that includes Ganna. 2026-04-12T12:29:55.018ZPithie bouncing his bike to check if he has a puncture. 2026-04-12T12:30:37.489ZGanna only has Jordi Meeus (Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe) with him just 19" off the front. 2026-04-12T12:31:05.550ZVan der Poel comes to the front of the main chase group and is now over two minutes down. 2026-04-12T12:32:30.627ZVan der Poel now has Philipsen to help him with a few other riders working hard for their own chances. 2026-04-12T12:32:57.229ZGanna and Meeus are now just 5" off the front group with 85km to go. 2026-04-12T12:35:21.663Z Sector 17, Hornaing à Wandignies Pogačar (UAD)Van Aert (TVL)Laporte (TVL)Pedersen (LTK)Ganna (IGD)Pithie (RBH)Meeus (RBH)Stuyven (SOQ)Bissegger (DCT) Chase group 1 +41"Van der Poel group +1'39" 2026-04-12T12:37:09.479ZAnother puncture for Ganna who has given so much to get back to the front is now out the back again as Pogačar is really pushing on this four star sector. 2026-04-12T12:38:20.693ZPhilipsen leads Van der Poel onto sector 17 and the defending champion looks locked in and is very focused. 2026-04-12T12:39:04.344Z80km to go as Ganna is now over 40 seconds back. Van der Poel is slowly closing the gap at 1'27" now. 2026-04-12T12:39:50.132ZPogačar is giving it a lot of welly on this sector as Meeus is being distanced after all the work he did with Ganna to get back in. 2026-04-12T12:40:29.094ZVan der Poel has Politt, Brennan, Turner and a couple of others on his wheel, but he has destroyed that chase group. 2026-04-12T12:41:18.030ZVan der Poel drops Brennan and catches Milan, but Pogačar has dragged the gap back to 1'33" as Van Aert comes through at the front. 2026-04-12T12:41:46.362ZPithie with a puncture! Meeus stops to give him his wheel. 2026-04-12T12:42:51.306ZMeeus and Pithie now both riding with the Belgian sprinter working for his leader who has looked in amazing form. 2026-04-12T12:43:43.058ZLeaders have 49" on Pithie and Meeus then 1'06" to the Ineos led Ganna group and then 1'33" to the Van der Poel group. 2026-04-12T12:45:07.829Z Sector 16, Warlaing à Brillon 2026-04-12T12:45:38.400ZVan der Poel has Politt, Heiduk and Milan on his wheel. Three riders who will absolutely not work with him. 2026-04-12T12:46:15.734ZPIthie leads Meeus behind on the Warlaing à Brillon as he tries to get back to the leaders. 2026-04-12T12:47:10.681ZVan der Poel is flying, just 1'27" further back than where he wants to be.
